title: Bean Burrito
subtitle: Spiced black bean and rice burrito
excerpt: Spiced black beans and rice wrapped in a large flour tortilla with Cheddar, soured cream, and coriander. A filling vegan main that comes together in 20 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Burritos are a Tex-Mex and Northern Mexican staple: a large flour tortilla wrapped tightly around a filling of meat, beans, rice, and cheese. The vegetarian version using black beans or pinto beans became popular in British food culture from the 1990s onwards. Mission-style burritos from San Francisco typically include both rice and beans in the wrap, which provides a complete protein and makes the burrito substantial enough to serve as a full meal.

content.text: Warm the tortillas before filling: cold tortillas crack when rolled. Wrap each burrito tightly in foil immediately after assembling to keep it together. For a toasted burrito, place the foil-wrapped burrito seam-side down in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.

Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Meanwhile, heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained black beans. Stir to coat in the spices. Add 100 ml of water and simmer for 5 minutes until the beans are heated through and the sauce is thick. Add the lime juice. Season with salt.
Warm each tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side or wrap the stack in foil and place in a warm oven for 5 minutes.

Spread a spoonful of soured cream in the centre of each tortilla. Add a scoop of rice, then the spiced beans. Sprinkle with cheese and coriander. Fold the sides in, then roll from the bottom up into a tight cylinder. Serve immediately.
